newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - OCT 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - OCT 16.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Cabinet makes clear to newly-appointed regional and ministry secretary-generals that it is not acceptable for them to use their positions as springboards to elections to Parliament. However, there are questions as to whether this is legally enforceable.

--European Commission report says Athens leads European capitals in pollution levels and calls on government to take additional measures to replace old vehicles and as well as ensure better fuel quality. At the same time, environment deputy minister Theodoros Koliopanos asks for year's exemption for Greece from law phasing out leaded petrol.
--Education ministry needs "excessive" for 1997 budget, economic team tells Prime Minister Costas Simitis.
--TV spectacle over the case of an eight-year-old street kid found unconscious on a beach on Sunday.

--Appointment of leading publisher Stavros Psyharis as governor of the autonomous monastic community of Mount Athos technically null and void as it was made under a non-existent law. Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos insists on his decision but the monks of Athos continue to object.
--An omen for Greece? Spain and France sees mass demonstrations against continuing austerity imposed by the needs of convergence.

--Communists favour taxation of state titles, but Democratic Social Movement leader Dimitris Tsovolas comes out against. Simitis expresses displeasure yesterday at public statements by ministers in favour of taxing bonds and T-bills.
--Homeless and at the mercy of gangs. The collapse of the eight-year-old brings to light the tragedy of a family.
--European Union's programme to replace leaded petrol vehicles with those using unleaded petrol will force Greece to introduce incentives.
--Alpha Credit makes overtures to merchants and industrialists with new low 14.0 percent loans for business. New interest rate war on the horizon.
--Education minister Gerasimos Arsenis denies tension with his predecessor George Papandreou but freezes all four education measures previously decided.
